History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
Young adult female with 2-day history of midline lower abdominal pain, mild nausea, urinary frequency, and pink-tinged urine; remote telehealth clinician suspects uncomplicated urinary tract infection and prescribes a 3-day oral antibiotic course.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Lower abdominal (“lower tummy”) pain for the last 2 days.  
• Location: Midline lower abdomen.  
• Character/progression: Constant pain; no prior similar episodes.  
• Associated urinary features:  
  – Slight pink discoloration of urine noted once.  
  – Mild increase in urinary frequency.  
  – No dysuria, no foul odor, no flank/back pain.  
• Constitutional/other associated symptoms:  
  – Feels intermittently “hot and sweaty,” but measured oral temperature ~37 °C one hour before consult; no documented fever spikes.  
  – Mild nausea; no vomiting.  
  – Increased thirst.  
• Gastrointestinal:  
  – Constipation last week, now resolved; normal bowel movement 2 h before consult.  
  – No diarrhea, no blood in stool, no upper-abdominal pain, no acid reflux.  
• Gynecologic:  
  – Regular menses.  
  – No inter-menstrual or post-coital bleeding.  
  – No abnormal vaginal discharge.  
• Exposures/travel: No recent travel abroad.  
• Review of systems otherwise non-contributory as per conversation.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic illnesses reported.  
• Prior contraceptive implant (removed; was in place for ~1 yr, now discontinued).  

Allergies:
• Amoxicillin – reaction type not specified.

Medications:
• None prescribed or over-the-counter.  
• (Contraceptive implant removed; not current therapy.)

Social History:
• Lives with parents.  
• Tobacco: Non-smoker.  
• Alcohol: ~1 beer on 4 days per week.  
• Recreational drugs: Not mentioned.

Family History:
• Mother – breast cancer (treated at early stage).  
• No other familial conditions discussed.

Physical Examination:
(Telehealth – no direct exam performed)  
• Reported temperature: 37 °C.  
• No additional vitals or physical findings documented.

Investigations:
• None obtained during this remote visit.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Suspected uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (UTI):
  • Assessment: Lower abdominal pain, urinary frequency, hematuria (pink urine), mild systemic symptoms without fever or flank pain; clinician suspects cystitis/UTI.  
  • Plan:  
    – Prescribe 3-day oral antibiotic, twice daily (specific agent not documented).  
    – Counsel patient to start medication immediately upon collection from nominated pharmacy.  
    – Safety-net advice: Seek urgent review if pain worsens, fever develops, flank/back pain appears, new symptoms arise, or no improvement after course; may require face-to-face examination.

Issue 2 – Drug allergy (Amoxicillin):
  • Assessment: Patient reports allergy to amoxicillin. Potential risk if penicillin-derivative antibiotic is chosen.  
  • Plan:  
    – Ensure prescribed antibiotic is non-penicillin based. (Not explicitly addressed in transcript—highlighted for prescribing clinician.)  
    – Document allergy prominently in record.

General plan items:
• No additional concerns; patient had no further questions.  
• Follow-up via telehealth or in-person as needed based on response to therapy or symptom progression.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Expected elements missing: detailed allergy reaction, complete vitals (BP, HR, RR, SpO₂), physical abdominal examination, urinalysis to confirm UTI, medication name/dose/route/frequency.  
• Internal conflicts: Antibiotic prescribed without specifying class despite known amoxicillin allergy – potential conflict noted.  
• Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional brief inaudible/overlapping speech but main clinical details discernible.
